hints: Follow the marble transfer rules carefully at each stage.

Stage 2 (from Bag B): if Red from Bag A was discarded, Bag B has 4 Red and 1 Blue (total 5): P(R) = 4/5, P(B) = 1/5. If Blue from Bag A was added, Bag B has 4 Red and 2 Blue (total 6): P(R) = 4/6 (or 2/3), P(B) = 2/6 (or 1/3).

Stage 3 (from Bag A): track Bag A's count after each stage: after RR, Bag A has 7 R, 3 B (P(R) = 7/10, P(B) = 3/10); after RB, Bag A has 7 R, 4 B (P(R) = 7/11, P(B) = 4/11); after BR, Bag A has 8 R, 2 B (P(R) = 8/10, P(B) = 2/10); after BB, Bag A has 8 R, 3 B (P(R) = 8/11, P(B) = 3/11).
walkthrough:
Complete the second stage from Bag B:
- After Red from Bag A: Bag B contains $4R, 1B$ (total 5) $\implies \mathrm{P}(R) = \frac{4}{5}, \; \mathrm{P}(B) = \frac{1}{5}$
- After Blue from Bag A: Bag B contains $4R, 2B$ (total 6) $\implies \mathrm{P}(R) = \frac{4}{6}, \; \mathrm{P}(B) = \frac{2}{6}$

Complete the third stage from Bag A:
- Following $R_A, R_B$: Bag A has $7R, 3B$ (total 10) $\implies \mathrm{P}(R) = \frac{7}{10}, \; \mathrm{P}(B) = \frac{3}{10}$
- Following $R_A, B_B$: Bag A has $7R, 4B$ (total 11) $\implies \mathrm{P}(R) = \frac{7}{11}, \; \mathrm{P}(B) = \frac{4}{11}$
- Following $B_A, R_B$: Bag A has $8R, 2B$ (total 10) $\implies \mathrm{P}(R) = \frac{8}{10}, \; \mathrm{P}(B) = \frac{2}{10}$
- Following $B_A, B_B$: Bag A has $8R, 3B$ (total 11) $\implies \mathrm{P}(R) = \frac{8}{11}, \; \mathrm{P}(B) = \frac{3}{11}$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Understand Bag contents and transfer rules:
- Bag A initially: 8 Red, 3 Blue (total 11).
- Bag B initially: 4 Red, 1 Blue (total 5).
- Draw 1 from Bag A: Red is discarded; Blue is put into Bag B.
- Draw 2 from Bag B: Red is discarded; Blue is put into Bag A.
- Draw 3 from Bag A: chosen from the updated contents of Bag A.

Step 2: Second stage branch probabilities (from Bag B):
- If first draw was Red: Bag B is untouched with 4 Red, 1 Blue ($5$ total):
  $$\mathrm{P}(R_B) = \frac{4}{5}, \quad \mathrm{P}(B_B) = \frac{1}{5}$$
- If first draw was Blue: Bag B now has 4 Red, 2 Blue ($6$ total):
  $$\mathrm{P}(R_B) = \frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}, \quad \mathrm{P}(B_B) = \frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}$$

Step 3: Third stage branch probabilities (from Bag A):
- Path $R_A, R_B$: Bag A lost 1 Red, gained nothing $\implies 7R, 3B$ ($10$ total):
  $$\mathrm{P}(R) = \frac{7}{10}, \quad \mathrm{P}(B) = \frac{3}{10}$$
- Path $R_A, B_B$: Bag A lost 1 Red, gained 1 Blue $\implies 7R, 4B$ ($11$ total):
  $$\mathrm{P}(R) = \frac{7}{11}, \quad \mathrm{P}(B) = \frac{4}{11}$$
- Path $B_A, R_B$: Bag A lost 1 Blue, gained nothing $\implies 8R, 2B$ ($10$ total):
  $$\mathrm{P}(R) = \frac{8}{10}, \quad \mathrm{P}(B) = \frac{2}{10}$$
- Path $B_A, B_B$: Bag A lost 1 Blue, gained 1 Blue $\implies 8R, 3B$ ($11$ total):
  $$\mathrm{P}(R) = \frac{8}{11}, \quad \mathrm{P}(B) = \frac{3}{11}$$

hints: All three marbles chosen are the same colour corresponds to RRR or BBB.
walkthrough: Identify the two mutually exclusive paths with all three marbles of the same colour ($RRR$ and $BBB$):

Multiply the probabilities along the $RRR$ path:
$$\mathrm{P}(RRR) = \frac{8}{11} \times \frac{4}{5} \times \frac{7}{10} = \frac{224}{550} = \frac{112}{275}$$

Multiply the probabilities along the $BBB$ path:
$$\mathrm{P}(BBB) = \frac{3}{11} \times \frac{2}{6} \times \frac{3}{11} = \frac{18}{726} = \frac{3}{121}$$

Add the two path probabilities:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{all same colour}) = \frac{112}{275} + \frac{3}{121} = \frac{1307}{3025} \approx 0.432\text{ (3 s.f.)}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Identify the two paths where all 3 marbles have the same colour:
Path 1: All Red ($R_1 \cap R_2 \cap R_3$)
Path 2: All Blue ($B_1 \cap B_2 \cap B_3$)
These paths are mutually exclusive.

Step 2: Evaluate the Red path:
$$\mathrm{P}(RRR) = \mathrm{P}(R_1) \times \mathrm{P}(R_2 \mid R_1) \times \mathrm{P}(R_3 \mid R_1 \cap R_2)$$
$$\mathrm{P}(RRR) = \frac{8}{11} \times \frac{4}{5} \times \frac{7}{10} = \frac{224}{550} = \frac{112}{275}$$

Step 3: Evaluate the Blue path:
$$\mathrm{P}(BBB) = \mathrm{P}(B_1) \times \mathrm{P}(B_2 \mid B_1) \times \mathrm{P}(B_3 \mid B_1 \cap B_2)$$
$$\mathrm{P}(BBB) = \frac{3}{11} \times \frac{2}{6} \times \frac{3}{11} = \frac{18}{726} = \frac{3}{121}$$

Step 4: Sum the probabilities:
$$\mathrm{P}(\text{all same}) = \frac{112}{275} + \frac{3}{121}$$
Common denominator is $25 \times 11^2 = 3025$:
$$\frac{112 \times 11}{3025} + \frac{3 \times 25}{3025} = \frac{1232 + 75}{3025} = \frac{1307}{3025}$$
Convert to decimal form:
$$\frac{1307}{3025} = 0.432066\dots \approx 0.432\text{ (3 s.f.)}$$
